label: first copy-phase step after <DEL> in length-9 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase and almost only at the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx == 1, so the input is the fed-back first original token). It is strongly tied to length: for L=9 (t=10) it fires on about 66% of sequences and holds about 91% of activation mass. For L=8 (t=9) it fires on about 11% of sequences, weakly (about 8% of mass). It almost never fires for L<=7, in the original or delimiter phases, or at later copy steps. Within L=9 sequences, which ones fire depends weakly on token identity. The top activations have first token v or w (v has the highest rate), and the rate rises somewhat with the number of digits. No simple token rule separates the roughly 34% of L=9 sequences that stay below threshold. Overall it reads like a position/length timer for the first recall step of the longest sequences.
